key_insight: Ropedia W0 introduces a shared world model for anticipating movement and object-interaction outcomes across humans and different robot bodies. Its central idea is to combine large-scale first-person human experience with robot data.
problem_solved: Humans and robots have different action spaces, making it difficult to build one model that predicts both locomotion and manipulation across embodiments. Limited multimodal training data adds to this challenge.
method: Develop an egocentric world foundation model spanning human and diverse robot embodiments.
Curate Xp-Data with 10,000 hours of first-person human data and 3,000 hours of robot data.
Use unified multimodal annotations to support joint modeling of locomotion and manipulation.
impact: This approach could help practitioners use human experience to train more broadly applicable robot world models. The supplied abstract is truncated, so performance gains and transfer capabilities cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Human and multiple robot icons feeding into one shared world model.

paper_title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
paper_authors: Tianqi Liu, Hanfei Zhao, Qifeng Liang, Hui En Pang, Jiarui Xu
